Statement: “a weak and ruined fort consisting of a lower fort and a citadel”
Measurement or test: Two enclosures: lower fort and a separate three-ring citadel mound 530 m to the SW

Statement: “The lower fort ... occupied one-sixth of the space of Belgaum fort”
Measurement or test: Implied 6.7-9.7 ha; measured lower-fort enclosure 13.37 (12.53-14.26) ha

Statement: “The upper fort or citadel, with a deep quarry in its centre had one-tenth the area of Belgaum fort”
Measurement or test: Implied 4.0-5.8 ha; measured outer ring 6.92 (6.51-7.38) ha, middle ring 3.78 (3.55-4.02) ha
No central depression resolved: stereo core centre minus rim +2.4 m (noise c. 8 m)

Statement: “The upper battery was a strong citadel nowhere commanded though conspicuous for many miles in every direction”
Measurement or test: Copernicus: 2 cells within 1 km exceed the summit by 0.1 m; first ground > 1 m higher: 787 m at 1.5-2 km; 153 km² visible within 25 km

Statement: “Near it is a ditch about sixteen feet deep ... About eighty yards beyond is a second ditch and remains of the fort walls”
Measurement or test: 80 yd = 73 m. Spacing of the N/W moat line from the enclosure: median 123 m (5-95%: 36-195 m); east outer line 54 m (49-81 m)

Statement: “an advanced fortified post was carried. On this post a battery was raised which next day effected a practical breach”
Measurement or test: Not locatable; illustrative zone within 150 m of an assumed East Gate: 4.0 ha

Source: Deacon to Pierce and Trewman, 8 Dec 1824 (NAI Foreign Political (Secret) Cons. 7 Jan 1825 No. 17)
Statement: “the most advanced Post, nearest to the East [?] Gate ... I advanced repeatedly close to the Crest of the Glacis”
Measurement or test: Glacis crest zone 30-100 m from the east face: 2.8 ha (construction)

Source: Trewman, 8 Dec 1824 (NAI Foreign Political (Secret) Cons. 7 Jan 1825 No. 17)
Statement: “entered the Works by escalade between the lower, and the Upper Fort”
Measurement or test: Gap between the lower fort and the citadel mound: 4.9 ha (construction)

Statement: “about 1000 yards long and 800 yards broad ... 2900 yards perimeter ... about 100 acres”
Measurement or test: 914 x 732 m, 2652 m; 100 acres = 40.5 ha, but an oval of the stated dimensions encloses 52.5 ha. Traced on DA222 (1968): 876 x 846 m, moat centreline perimeter 2831 m, inner wall line 58.0 ha, moat outer edge 64.8 ha (OSM outline 51.8 ha)
